items.title: The U.S.’ Own Goal: Why World Cup Expectations Deflated
items.summary: World Cup host cities were promised a once-in-a-generation tourism surge. The lift is real, but some cities’ results are well below expectations.

items.title: Why Hotel AI Keeps Cutting Costs Instead of Making Money
items.summary: AI can't sell what hotel systems can't see. Until room-level data, guest behavior, and service pricing live in one connected system, the industry's AI gains will stay stuck on the cost efficiency side of the ledger.

items.title: Canada Is Looking for a New Caribbean. Most Destinations Are Not Ready to Be Found
items.summary: Canada's three winter sun standbys — the U.S., Cuba, and Mexico — are all in trouble at the same time. The Caribbean has never had a better opening. Most destinations are not ready to walk through it.

items.title: Delta Expands Travel Benefits on Amex Cards, Holds Fees Steady
items.summary: Delta is not hiking fees on its credit cards even as its competitors continue to increase annual fees and roll out premium travel credit cards in an increasingly saturated market.

items.title: Dubai Turns to New Visitors and Events to Ride Out Iran War Tourism Slump
items.summary: Every tool is in play. What’s missing is a lasting ceasefire.

items.title: Why These Operators Are Skipping the Pilot Phase
items.summary: The hospitality companies scaling AI fast aren't running better pilots. They've stopped thinking in pilots at all.

items.title: The Best AI Goes Unnoticed: Perk CPO Nikita Miller on the Future of Business Travel
items.summary: For Skift IDEA Awards Judge Nikita Miller, the real measure of success in travel and technology isn't the sophistication of the AI — it's the human time and judgment it gives back.

items.title: Booking.com CTO: The New Bottleneck Is Teamwork
items.summary: Many of the pressing issues in AI implementation are organizational, not technological.
